content: Lansoprazole can cause allergic reactions, some of which may be severe. If you experience any of the following symptoms, stop taking lansoprazole immediately and seek medical attention: difficulty breathing or wheezing, a rapid heartbeat, fever or a general feeling of being unwell, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing or a sensation of throat tightness, itching, skin rash, or pale red bumps on the skin (hives), nausea or vomiting, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, stomach cramps, or joint pain. Individuals who are allergic to lansoprazole, any of its brand names (Prevacid, Prevacid SoluTabs, Prevacid 24HR), other proton pump inhibitors, or any ingredients in the specific product should not use lansoprazole. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients in the product. Lansoprazole may interact with other medications. Before starting lansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Certain medications, such as methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, theophylline, clarithromycin, tacrolimus, antiretroviral drugs (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin, may interact with lansoprazole. These interactions can alter the effectiveness or blood levels of lansoprazole or the other medications. Always discuss your medication history with your healthcare provider. Do not take lansoprazole unless it has been prescribed to you by a healthcare provider. Take it exactly as prescribed and do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms, as it may harm them. Keep lansoprazole out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush the capsules. Take lansoprazole before a meal. Antacids may be used alongside lansoprazole if needed. If you are also taking sucralfate, take lansoprazole at least 30 minutes before sucralfate. Lansoprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to achieve full effect. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsule, you may open it and sprinkle the contents on one tablespoon of applesauce, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. Swallow the mixture immediately without chewing and do not mix it with other foods. If administered via a nasogastric (NG) tube, follow your healthcare provider’s instructions. Lansoprazole SoluTabs contain phenylalanine, a component of aspartame, which may be a concern for individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU). Children under one year of age may be at greater risk for certain side effects. Discuss the risks with your healthcare provider if your child is under one year old. Before using lansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions, including low blood potassium (hypokalemia), low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia), low blood calcium (hypocalcemia), low blood sodium (hyponatremia), liver problems, or phenylketonuria. This information will help your provider determine if lansoprazole is appropriate for you. Lansoprazole may affect the absorption of certain medications. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications and supplements you are taking or have recently taken. This list may not include all possible interactions, so consult your provider for more details. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. It is not known if lansoprazole can harm an unborn baby. Your provider will advise you on whether to use lansoprazole during pregnancy. Do not take lansoprazole while breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk. Store lansoprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). It can be exposed to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) for short periods, such as during transportation. The most common side effects of lansoprazole include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, and constipation. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, while less common, include kidney problems (e.g., acute tubulointerstitial nephritis), antibiotic-associated diarrhea (e.g., Clostridioides difficile infection), severe skin reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), lupus, vitamin B-12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia, and bone loss or fractures. If you experience symptoms such as decreased urine output, blood in urine, watery or persistent diarrhea, severe stomach cramps, fever, painful or peeling skin, rash, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, joint pain, sore tongue, weakness, tingling or numbness in extremities, changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures, stop using lansoprazole and contact your healthcare provider immediately. If you accidentally take too much lansoprazole, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Lansoprazole is used to treat heartburn and conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and Helicobacter pylori infections. It works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. It is available in delayed-release oral capsules (15 mg and 30 mg) and orally disintegrating tablets (15 mg and 30 mg).
